hook: Directed graphs can be sparsified to about n log n arcs, down from n log^5 n, keeping every degree.
summary: A singular-value sparsifier reweights a subset of a directed graph's arcs so degrees are exactly preserved while matrix behavior is approximately kept. The paper proves that O(n log n / epsilon^2) arcs always suffice, improving the earlier log^5 n bound, and gives a randomized construction running in near-linear time. This is a theoretical bound with no experiments reported.
title: Directed Singular-Value Sparsifiers with $O(n \log n/\epsilon^2)$ Arcs
